name: kaldrax_public_repository_engineering_v1

privacy_screening.scope: Public main-branch files only; no local SQLite databases, .kaldrax runtime reports, secrets, environment values, private conversation content, or private repositories were read.
privacy_screening.note: This is a source-scope screen, not a human privacy approval. Review every source path and content before treating the corpus as approved.

annotation_rubric: Each query has an assistant-proposed relevant-memory set and rationale. A human reviewer must confirm, amend, or reject every set before reporting these scores as human-labeled results.

memories.content: KALDRAX is a local-first Python engineering application: the local control plane owns orchestration, policy, persistent memory, and run reports, while model providers are adapters.
memories.summary: Local Python control plane owns orchestration and memory.

memories.content: Persistent project memory is stored in the local SQLite database at .kaldrax/memory.sqlite3 by default.
memories.summary: Default durable memory database is local SQLite.

source.anchor: Quick start; Memory persistence and schema evolution

memories.content: Memory reads are scoped by project ID; an agent sees its own private records plus project-shared records, not another agent's private memories.
memories.summary: Project scope and agent-private visibility rules.

memories.content: The acceptance evaluator receives the original task contract and candidate artifact, but it does not receive retrieved memory context; memory cannot alter evaluator policy or acceptance criteria.
memories.summary: Evaluator is isolated from historical memory.

source.anchor: Execution with memory; Trust, privacy and local-first constraints

memories.content: When KALDRAX_EMBEDDING_MODEL is configured, the hosted OpenAI-compatible embeddings adapter sends project-memory text to the configured HTTPS provider; when it is unset, KALDRAX uses lexical retrieval and makes no embedding requests.
memories.summary: Hosted embeddings transmit memory text; lexical mode needs no embedding API.

memories.content: KALDRAX compares a stored memory vector with a query vector only when their hosted embedding endpoint/model identifiers match; changing the model or endpoint requires explicit reindexing.
memories.summary: Vectors require the same hosted endpoint/model identity and explicit reindexing after changes.

memories.content: Hybrid memory retrieval combines lexical token overlap and embedding cosine similarity, then adjusts relevance using memory confidence and age-based freshness.
memories.summary: Ranking mixes lexical, semantic, confidence, and freshness signals.

memories.content: LLM-extracted semantic memories are stored as pending proposals and are excluded from normal retrieval until a human reviewer approves them.
memories.summary: Extracted knowledge requires human approval.

memories.content: Each LLM-extracted memory must include an exact substring from the candidate artifact, at least 12 characters long and containing at least three meaningful tokens.
memories.summary: Evidence quotes must be exact, substantive candidate substrings.

memories.content: Extractor confidence is defined as the model's conservative estimated probability that the whole claim is accurate, candidate-supported, and durable; the model-reported value is retained for evaluation.
memories.summary: Confidence meaning is defined and original score preserved.

memories.content: Default retention is 365 days for episodic memories and 180 days for semantic memories.
memories.summary: Memory lifetimes vary by memory type.

memories.content: Search excludes records whose expiry deadline has passed even before the maintenance command marks their persisted status as expired.
memories.summary: Expiry deadline is enforced at retrieval time.

memories.content: Contradiction candidates cover 13 opposition dimensions including allow/deny, public/private, local/cloud, online/offline, sync/async, mutable/immutable, retain/delete, include/exclude, required/optional, accept/reject, automatic/manual, encrypted/plaintext, and strict/fail-open.
memories.summary: Conflict detector covers 13 opposing policy dimensions.

memories.content: A contradiction candidate requires an opposing cue plus subject Jaccard similarity of at least 0.42, or optional same-batch hosted embedding cosine similarity of at least 0.84 for paraphrases; when hosted embeddings fail, detection falls back to lexical subject overlap.
memories.summary: Conflict detection uses opposition cues plus lexical or hosted-embedding thresholds.

memories.content: Conflict analysis treats explicit environment scopes such as production and staging as boundaries and filters pairs that refer to different environments.
memories.summary: Different explicit deployment environments are not conflicting by default.

memories.content: The contradiction detector does not compare agent-private memories owned by different agents.
memories.summary: Private memories from different agents are isolated during conflict analysis.

memories.content: Detected memory contradictions are review candidates only; KALDRAX never activates, supersedes, or resolves either side automatically, and a human must choose the outcome.
memories.summary: A person resolves every detected conflict.

memories.content: Retrieval benchmark execution creates a temporary SQLite database and does not seed, read, or mutate the operator's project memory database.
memories.summary: Benchmarks run against an isolated temporary store.

memories.content: The retrieval report includes Recall@k, Precision@k, NDCG@k, mean reciprocal rank, top-1 accuracy, and per-category aggregates.
memories.summary: Retrieval quality is reported with ranking and category metrics.

memories.content: The bundled engineering retrieval fixture contains 40 synthetic-curated memories and 42 queries across 15 categories; it is a regression fixture, not production workload evidence.
memories.summary: Current broad retrieval corpus is synthetic and limited.

memories.content: The expanded synthetic memory-extraction evaluation corpus contains 30 cases and 70 assistant-proposed expected claims; its labels require human review before validation or release use.
memories.summary: Extraction benchmark has 30 cases and 70 proposed claims awaiting human review.

source.anchor: The expanded candidate fixtures now meet the numerical size floors

memories.content: Extraction evaluation reports precision, recall, F1, exact-evidence quote validity, Brier score, and five-bin expected calibration error with reliability-bin accuracy.
memories.summary: Extractor quality and confidence calibration metrics.

memories.content: Brier score and expected calibration error on the synthetic extraction benchmark are descriptive regression diagnostics only; they do not establish production or population-wide confidence calibration, and proposed expected claims remain subject to human review.
memories.summary: Synthetic extraction calibration metrics are descriptive, not production evidence.

memories.content: All provider roles in one KALDRAX task or team run share a single thread-safe RunBudget for provider calls, input tokens, output tokens, total tokens, and wall-clock duration.
memories.summary: One budget is shared across every model role in a run.

memories.content: Default run limits are 20 provider calls, 60,000 estimated input tokens, 12,000 completion tokens, 72,000 total tokens, and 600 seconds of wall-clock time.
memories.summary: Default shared call, token, and duration ceilings.

memories.content: When a provider omits token-usage metadata, KALDRAX estimates token usage from UTF-8 prompt and output byte counts; those values are explicitly estimates rather than exact tokenization.
memories.summary: Missing provider usage falls back to byte-based estimates.

memories.content: Estimated monetary ceilings are optional and require operator-supplied input and output token prices per million; the estimate is not an invoice or guarantee of provider billing.
memories.summary: Cost accounting uses operator-provided rates and is approximate.

memories.content: The Python sandbox uses a disposable workspace, disabled container networking, read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, an unprivileged UID, and CPU, memory, PID, time, and output limits.
memories.summary: Sandbox restricts networking, privileges, and resources.

memories.content: The sandbox expects an operator-prepulled python:3.13-slim image and invokes Docker with pull disabled, so it does not fetch an image during execution.
memories.summary: Sandbox uses a pre-pulled fixed image and --pull=never.

memories.content: The bounded coordinator runs sequentially in planner, builder, reviewer, then independent evaluator order; it is not a distributed scheduler.
memories.summary: Team roles execute in a fixed sequential graph.

memories.content: Planner, builder, reviewer, and evaluator require four distinct configured model identifiers, and all role clients share the same run budget.
memories.summary: Four distinct model IDs are required for team orchestration.

memories.content: Reviewer approval is necessary but cannot override the independent evaluator, which judges the original task contract and immutable acceptance criteria.
memories.summary: Final acceptance authority remains with the independent evaluator.

memories.content: Workspace-backed team and DAG workflows can stage and verify a repository patch and apply it to the selected clean working tree only with explicit authorization; KALDRAX never creates a Git commit or pushes the result.
memories.summary: Repository workflows can explicitly apply verified patches but never commit or push.

source.anchor: The apply flag modifies the working tree but does not create a Git commit

memories.content: KALDRAX uses an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions transport through the Python standard library and does not require a provider-specific SDK.
memories.summary: Provider transport is SDK-independent and OpenAI-compatible.

source.anchor: v0.2 LLM executor and evidence evaluator

memories.content: The live provider smoke job is manually dispatched and secret-gated; ordinary push and pull-request test jobs do not require provider credentials.
memories.summary: Live provider checks are optional and manual.

memories.content: The regular GitHub Actions test matrix runs Python 3.11 and Python 3.13, runs the full pytest suite and regression benchmarks, and performs a real Docker smoke run on Python 3.13.
memories.summary: CI tests Python 3.11 and 3.13 and includes Docker smoke.

memories.content: The deterministic phrase evaluator regression fixture contains known false positives for negated statements such as saying a test was not run; benchmark success does not establish semantic reliability.
memories.summary: Deterministic evaluator has known negation false positives.

queries.query: Which part of KALDRAX owns orchestration, policy and durable engineering memory?
queries.rationale: Paraphrase of the documented local control-plane responsibility.

queries.query: Where does the default project knowledge database live on disk?
queries.rationale: Asks for the documented default SQLite path.

queries.query: Can one agent retrieve another agent's private run notes?
queries.rationale: Targets the agent-private versus project-shared visibility contract.

queries.query: Does the final acceptance judge get to read recalled memory lessons?
queries.rationale: Targets the evaluator's memory isolation boundary.

queries.query: What happens to project-memory content when hosted semantic embeddings are enabled?
queries.rationale: The hosted embedding adapter sends input memory text to the configured HTTPS provider; without it, retrieval remains lexical.

queries.query: What must be done after changing the hosted embedding model or endpoint before searching existing vectors?
queries.rationale: Targets the endpoint/model identity rule and explicit reindexing requirement.

queries.query: Which signals determine the final ordering of recalled project knowledge?
queries.rationale: Targets the combined lexical, vector, confidence and freshness scoring.

queries.query: Can automatically extracted lessons affect the next run before review?
queries.rationale: Targets pending state and explicit approval gate.

queries.query: What makes a proposed memory's supporting evidence acceptable?
queries.rationale: Targets exact source substring and meaningful quote constraints.

queries.query: What does an extractor's confidence number claim to estimate?
queries.rationale: Targets the defined semantics of the model-reported score.

queries.query: How long are episodic and semantic memories retained by default?
queries.rationale: Targets memory-type-specific TTL defaults.

queries.query: Can an overdue memory still appear in search until a cleanup command runs?
queries.rationale: Targets expiry enforcement at search time.

queries.query: Which opposing policy types can trigger a memory contradiction candidate?
queries.rationale: Targets the opposition dimension list.

queries.query: How similar do two statements need to be before opposing language is considered a conflict?
queries.rationale: Targets lexical and optional embedding thresholds.

queries.query: Should a staging rule that differs from production automatically conflict with it?
queries.rationale: Targets environment-boundary filtering.

queries.query: Are private notes owned by two different agents cross-compared for contradictions?
queries.rationale: Targets agent-private isolation during conflict analysis.

queries.query: Does KALDRAX automatically choose which contradictory memory should remain active?
queries.rationale: Targets the human-only conflict resolution safeguard.

queries.query: Will running the retrieval test add fixtures to my actual project memory database?
queries.rationale: Targets the temporary benchmark database isolation.

queries.query: Which ranking quality measures does the memory search benchmark output?
queries.rationale: Targets the full set of retrieval metrics.

queries.query: How much real-world evidence do the currently bundled engineering search queries provide?
queries.rationale: Targets synthetic dataset size and its limitations.

queries.query: How many cases and proposed expected claims are in the current memory-extraction benchmark?
queries.rationale: Targets the current expanded corpus size and keeps the proposed-label status explicit.

queries.query: How does the extractor benchmark check whether confidence scores are calibrated?
queries.rationale: Metrics and sample-size qualification are both relevant.

queries.query: Do planner, reviewer and evaluator each receive independent API spending limits?
queries.rationale: Targets one shared budget across all roles.

queries.query: What are the out-of-the-box call, token and duration caps for a run?
queries.rationale: Targets the default RunBudget values.

queries.query: What does KALDRAX do if the model API does not return token counts?
queries.rationale: Targets byte-based approximate accounting.

queries.query: Are estimated provider costs an exact invoice from the API company?
queries.rationale: Targets optional cost ceiling and its limitations.

queries.query: How is candidate Python execution isolated from the host and network?
queries.rationale: Targets the container isolation controls.

queries.query: Does running the sandbox automatically download its container image?
queries.rationale: Targets pre-pull and --pull=never behavior.

queries.query: In what order do the four roles collaborate on a bounded engineering task?
queries.rationale: Targets the sequential planner-builder-reviewer-evaluator graph.

queries.query: Can the same model identifier be assigned to planner and reviewer?
queries.rationale: Targets distinct role-model configuration.

queries.query: Can a reviewer approve a result that the independent acceptance evaluator rejects?
queries.rationale: Targets final evaluator authority.

queries.query: Does the multi-role coordinator commit source code changes directly to Git?
queries.rationale: The query asks about commits; the current repository workflow can apply a patch but explicitly never commits or pushes.

queries.query: Does the core require the OpenAI Python client package to call chat models?
queries.rationale: Targets provider-neutral standard-library transport.

queries.query: Will every pull request call the configured paid LLM provider during CI?
queries.rationale: Targets secret-gated, manual provider checks.

queries.query: Which Python versions are exercised by the hosted test matrix?
queries.rationale: Targets the CI matrix configuration.

queries.query: What known weakness remains in the deterministic acceptance checker when text says tests were not run?
queries.rationale: Targets the known negation false-positive limitation.
